current_activity: lands over the Ouistreham beaches; reaches the airborne area east of the Orne in the afternoon
notes: Event date: 6 June 1944 (Stacey, p. 117: "In the afternoon of D Day"). Event definition: The commandos of the brigade, under Brigadier Lord Lovat, land over the Ouistreham beaches (Queen Red, the easternmost sector of Sword), No. 4 Commando clearing targets in Ouistreham; in the afternoon they reach the 6th Airborne Division's area and start mopping up the coast defences east of the Orne (Stacey, p. 117; Wikipedia). Event support: two source families (Stacey, the Canadian official history, and Wikipedia). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 117: "In the afternoon of D Day the commandos of the 1st Special Service Brigade, commanded by Brigadier Lord Lovat, which had landed over the Ouistreham beaches, arrived in the airborne troops"; Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade: "to land at Ouistreham in Queen Red sector (the most easterly)"; "moving inland to join-up with the 6th Airborne Division". Location: Ouistreham, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Ouistreham; the brigade landed on the beaches by it and moved inland east of the Orne the same afternoon. Location support: Stacey names the Ouistreham beaches (p. 117); Wikipedia names Queen Red sector at Ouistreham. Commander: Brigadier The Lord Lovat, wounded 12 June 1944; then Brigadier Derek Mills-Roberts (Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade; Stacey, p. 117). current_activity: Blackcock: under the 7th Armoured Division, clears the country along the Maas north of Echt
notes: Event date: about 20 January 1945 (approximate: Ellis, vol. Event definition: Back from England, the brigade (renamed the 1st Commando Brigade) comes under the 7th Armoured Division from VIII Corps during Operation Blackcock; the division sweeps north-east from Echt while the commandos clear the country next to the Maas (Ellis, vol. Wikipedia says the brigade was temporarily under the 7th Armoured Division and names Brachterbeek, where Lance Corporal Harden of No. 45 (Royal Marine) Commando won a posthumous Victoria Cross. Location: Brachterbeek, Maasgouw, Limburg (NL) (new place) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Brachterbeek, on the Maas north of Echt; the brigade cleared the river country there. current_activity: crosses the Rhine about two miles downstream of Wesel and attacks the town after the bombing
notes: Event date: 23 March 1945, from 10 p.m. (Stacey, p. 535; Ellis, vol. II, p. 289: an hour after the 51st Division's assault). Event definition: An hour after the 51st Division's assault, the brigade of XII Corps crosses the Rhine about two miles downstream of Wesel, beginning at 10 p.m., with one commando in Buffaloes forming a bridgehead and another by stormboat leading the assault on Wesel, which Bomber Command then hits with about 1,100 tons of bombs (Ellis, vol. II, p. 289; Stacey, p. 535); Wikipedia puts the crossing about 1.5 km north of Wesel. Event support: three source families (Ellis, the British official history, and Stacey, the Canadian official history, and Wikipedia). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 289: "the 1st Commando Brigade of XII Corps crossed about two miles downstream of Wesel"; Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 535: "the 1st Commando Brigade established itself immediately west of Wesel, beginning its crossing at 10:00 p.m."; Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Brigade: "then the 1st Commando Brigade, 1.5 km north of Wesel". Location: Wesel, North Rhine-Westphalia (PL0632) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town; the brigade crossed just downstream of it and attacked into it. Location support: Ellis and Stacey place the crossing just downstream (west) of Wesel and the assault on the town.
